card.intuition: Inference is running a trained model to generate output — what happens on every model provider request, with parameters held fixed. It is cheap relative to training but billed per token and is the dominant cost of using a model. Training already happened once, but inference costs accrue every time anyone runs the model.
card.analogy: Running a packaged compiler on each file you give it: the compiler was authored once, but every invocation consumes machine time billed to you, and the compiler never incorporates your earlier files.
card.time_complexity: Cost scales with input + output tokens per model provider request; an agent doing many tool calls pays for inference on each round trip, so a single turn can expand into many charged requests.
card.space_complexity: The context window holds a fixed token budget — everything loaded competes for it and overflow means truncation, compaction, or handoff; continuity must come from outside the model.
when_to_use: Explaining why the bill scales with usage instead of being a flat license
Accounting for tool-call loops that expand one turn into many requests
Choosing a context window or memory system for continuity, since the model can't learn from a session
gotchas: Nothing you do at inference writes back to parameters — a correction today won't stick tomorrow
A model that repeats a mistake after you explained the fix hasn't ignored you; it's incapable of learning from the exchange
